entries.label: In lieu of a required cover letter, please describe why you are interested in interning at Hudl in 2-5 sentences.
entries.value: I want to work on software where there is a concrete user and a real failure mode, and Hudl's products sit with coaches and athletes who notice immediately when something is slow, wrong, or confusing. The work I am proudest of has that property: I built and shipped ClarityAtlas, an iOS health app, into a live pilot at Johns Hopkins with 30+ users, and I learned there that recruiting users and refining the product thesis mattered as much as the Swift and Supabase work behind it. I also build machine-learning systems where the output has to be useful to a human making a decision, including an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization core where too many alerts would just create a second problem. Hudl's internship appeals to me because it is a team that expects engineers to own real work rather than isolated tickets, and I would rather learn from people who hold a high bar than optimize for a more legible resume line.
